Space skipping and empty volume culling are acceleration techniques in image-order volume rendering that reduce computational load by identifying and bypassing regions of the volume or ray path that do not contribute to the final image [S2][S4, unofficial].

The evidence in Source [S4] explicitly describes an optimization where the marching algorithm previously visited every volume at every step, often finding it was not inside. The new method builds an 'active list up front' so that a step only visits volumes whose t-range contains it. This is described as 'pure work elimination.' This directly supports the claim that 'empty volume culling' (identifying and bypassing regions/volumes that do not contribute) is an acceleration technique that reduces computational load.
